methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $65M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Vulcan Elements is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by John Maslin and Piotr Kulik that has raised $65M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 9 companies—8 private and 1 public—spanning similar robotics and manufacturing stages, including Series B-stage firms Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B), alongside earlier-stage comparables like Walden Robotics ($1.1B).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression methodology uses the $65M total raised as a baseline proxy and applies a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier for Series A to subsequent-stage progression, implying $130M. Peer-median analysis across the 4-company robotics and manufacturing comp set yields a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range from $1.1B to $2.0B. The peer set spans both Series B and Seed stages, creating inherent compression around the $1.1B–$2.0B band.

Triangulating these two methods produces a range of $110M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $915M. The wide dispersion reflects the stage heterogeneity in comparable firms—particularly the 2.0B–1.1B spread between Series B leaders and Seed-stage peers. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x stage multiplier for this specific market and whether peer valuations reflect sustainable metrics or mark-to-market variance. The median estimate of $915M sits materially above stage-progression but substantially below the peer median, reflecting tension between backward-looking capital efficiency and peer-benchmarked expectations.
